Answer: C) Bibasal interstitial reticulonodular shadowing with peripheral distribution, consistent with interstitial lung disease.  
Reason: The original CXR shows bilateral, predominantly basal reticulonodular opacities that are more prominent peripherally (especially in the lower lung zones), with no clear cavitations, unilateral dominance, or diffuse alveolar ground-glass pattern; the “L” marker confirms patient left is on image right, and abnormalities are symmetrically bibasal—supporting option C over others requiring upper lobe, unilateral, central, or diffuse features.
